title: Free-variable output of the Razborov encoder is independent of its starting restriction
statement: Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables, a width $w$, a fuel bound, a decision path (a list of variable–direction pairs), and a base restriction $\rho_0$. The recursive worker of the Razborov encoding, run on these inputs together with a running restriction $\sigma$ and empty auxiliary data, returns among its outputs a restriction; write $R(\sigma)$ for this first output component. Let $v$ be a variable that is left free by $\rho_0$ and by two running restrictions $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, meaning $\rho_0(v)$, $\sigma_1(v)$, and $\sigma_2(v)$ are all undefined. Then the two runs agree at $v$: $R(\sigma_1)(v) = R(\sigma_2)(v)$.
hypotheses_covered: v is free under the base restriction ρ₀ (ρ₀ v = none)
v is free under σ₁ (σ₁ v = none)
v is free under σ₂ (σ₂ v = none)
shared inputs f, w, fuel, path, ρ₀, and empty auxiliary data
replaced:
At a variable $v$ that is free under $\rho_0$ and unset in both $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$,
the first component $\gamma$ of the encoder loop
\texttt{SwitchingLemma2.razborovEncode}'s \texttt{go} takes the same value at $v$ whether
started from $\sigma_1$ or $\sigma_2$.
